_note: Sources are tiered before any claim is read. Tier 0 and 4 are never crawled. Ranking is by whether the author bears a cost for being wrong. Seeded 2026-08-06.

tier_1_operators._rule: Authoritative for how their own system BEHAVES. Their performance claims are VENDOR-GOSPEL.

self_debunks.claim: Quality Score is an auction input you optimise
self_debunks.quote: Quality Score is not an input in the ad auction. It's a diagnostic tool.
Google Search does not provide special treatment such as ranking boosts ... including advertising.

tier_2_practitioners._rule: Harvest fully, claim-gate hard. Requires shown working: code, spend, timeframe, vertical or sample size.

recurring_studies.name: SearchPilot case studies
recurring_studies.why: Discloses its method: Bayesian credible intervals, bucketing into statistically similar control/variant groups, model confidence reported separately from results.
recurring_studies.caveat: Individual case studies are rigorous. Roundup posts list large uplifts with no confidence or method. Harvest the former only.

recurring_studies.name: Ahrefs GSC anonymised-query studies
recurring_studies.why: Primary data at scale, calculation disclosed, ships a reproducible template.
recurring_studies.caveat: INCENTIVE-CONFLICT: a tool vendor benefits when the data gap looks large.

recurring_studies.name: SparkToro zero-click
recurring_studies.why: Best limitations disclosure found; warns year-over-year comparison is shaky because the panel provider changed.
recurring_studies.caveat: Clickstream panel, not GSC. Never blend with GSC figures.

recurring_studies.name: Optmyzr match-type / bidding study
recurring_studies.why: Within-account comparison across thousands of accounts, caveats stated, and the author published a result against her own previously advocated position.
recurring_studies.caveat: Sample is an advanced tool's customer base.

recurring_studies.name: Advanced Web Ranking quarterly CTR
recurring_studies.why: Long consistent series, useful for direction of travel.
recurring_studies.caveat: No sample size and no stated data source. Never quote a precise figure as if the method were known.

tier_3_forums._rule: Only threads with visible correction dynamics and identifiable practitioners. single-source-pending at best.

tier_4_content_marketing._rule: Do not crawl. A single genuine teardown may be promoted by human decision.

tier_0_never._rule: SELLING or VENDOR-GOSPEL by construction. No exception path.

observed_denylist._note: Ranked on page one for exactly our topics while carrying no original data. Recorded because the harvester must never treat ranking as a quality signal: on these queries SERP position was anti-correlated with rigour, and the rigorous sources did not appear at all.

known_zombies._note: Figures that circulate detached from their method. Any claim resting on one is ECHO until traced to the original. Every one is the kind of thing an agency would happily put in a client deck.

claims.figure: 8-second attention span, worse than a goldfish
claims.reality: Traced through a 2015 corporate report to a stats aggregator whose own cited sources could find no record of the research when contacted.
Traced to a 1982 magazine advertising section, asserted with no citation. A public cash offer for supporting evidence went unclaimed.

claims.figure: People remember 10% of what they read
claims.reality: The percentages were never in the original work. Debunked repeatedly since 1971.
The documented pre-history says about twenty; the measured literature says three. Seven was fixed by a 1989 business book.

claims.figure: 5x more expensive to acquire than retain
claims.reality: Traced back through decades of citations and disappears.
From a 2004 study of 15 participants about health-site mistrust, not first impressions generally.
Traced to a 2015 agency blog recounting a personal count, itself an advert for that agency.
Two 1967 studies on single spoken words, combined. The author said it does not apply unless discussing feelings or attitudes.
Not fraudulent, but discloses no company, sample size, period, baseline, control, or how the figure was computed.

contested_not_settled._note: Live disagreements. Stored as contested, never client-facing. Stops us treating one side's confident post as settled.

items.state: Named practitioners argue both sides; neither has published a controlled test.
Credible statisticians disagree on whether a significant result from an underpowered test can be dismissed. Do not cite them as one voice.
No official documentation and no practitioner test found either way.

decay._note: Five tiers by half-life. The durability test: ask who would have to be wrong for this to stop being true. If the answer is one vendor's product manager, it is T1-T3 and must be re-verified against a primary source. If it is several independent replications across decades, it is T5. Advice written on the strength of an ANNOUNCEMENT decays far faster than advice written on the strength of a MEASUREMENT.

tiers.contents: where a button is, campaign-type names, which report exists
match-type semantics, crawler controls, consent posture
tiers.warning: often REVERSES. This tier produces confidently-wrong advice.
non-monotonic. Numbers rebound, so a stale figure can be wrong in EITHER direction.

tiers.contents: auction mechanics, intent stratification, incrementality vs correlation

source_hierarchy._note: Platform statements are NOT automatically top-tier. Spokespeople publicly denied mechanisms that a later confirmed document showed to exist. A claim resting on a single spokesperson post is weak evidence, not settled.
order: the platform's API changelog and release notes

provenance_trap._note: Track provenance at the DATA-SOURCE level, not the publisher level. Several apparently independent outlets share an owner or a measurement panel, so three 'independent' confirmations can be one clickstream. This is the ECHO check with teeth.
known_shared_ownership_or_panel: a major SEO tool vendor owns both a well-known research blog and a clickstream data provider
a widely cited zero-click study runs on a third party's panel
several experimentation tools have been absorbed by larger platforms

calibration_test._note: Use this as the acceptance test for any automated screen. Several sites published detailed, internally coherent, mutually corroborating analysis of a Google core update that never happened, complete with invented ranking factors and volatility figures. The status dashboard shows no such update.
calibration_test.lesson: Cross-site corroboration is NOT evidence when the sites generate from the same synthetic premise. Any screen that passes this fabricated update is not fit to run.

filter_rules._note: Each grounded in a traced case rather than intuition.
downgrade_or_reject: annualised from a short window (a month multiplied by twelve)
named subject absent ('a major retailer', 'a client in your industry')
proxy metric substituted for the outcome claimed (traffic quoted where revenue is the claim)
measurement instrument owned by the party with the conclusion
correlation study on SERP positions treated as ranking factors
citation depth under two hops to a primary source, or a terminal broken link
author identity unverifiable: no external footprint, stock or generated headshot, rotating bylines
no failure mode described (real practitioner writing names what did not work)
'the platform said X' resting on a single spokesperson post

vertical_literature._note: Searched specifically for luxury real estate, automotive dealer, dental and clinic marketing sources. That category is a funnel: nearly every result leads with paid coaching. This is a finding, not a search failure.
vertical_literature.structure: Take MECHANISM from horizontal sources, take demand-side data from trade associations, and let vertical specificity come from our own testing. Do not go looking for a dental-marketing publication.

reputation_warning._note: Reputation is the worst available filter. A large share of famous names are dormant, pivoted, or their domains now resolve to unrelated businesses and parked ad farms, while the reputation persists. A vault built from an old who-to-follow list points largely at corpses. Every source entry needs a last-verified date, not just a name.
